_comment: WP-2 fixture — RAW Selaras live-FG rows on the VERIFIED column list (tbl_1210,
2026-09-11): `kode_barang` (display only — the SO side has no such column),
The PRIMARY KEY is `tbl_1210_STLiveFGMX_id`; `sn_fg` is the ROLL SERIAL and is
kept as its own column — a row id is not what PPIC reads off a physical panel.
panel), `p`, `l`, `m2`, plus `deleted_at`. The two ACP Black Galaxy rolls sum
to 4,168 lembar, matching PRD §5A. Row 4 has an unreadable qty and row 5 has no
primary key: both must degrade, never abort the page. Row 6 carries SEPARATOR-
AMBIGUOUS quantities (A22). Row 7 carries NON-FINITE numerics (X11): NaN /
Infinity are legal Postgres numeric values, so they must be rejected at the
adapter, never written through. Row 9 is soft-deleted upstream (FIX 6) — and
it is the dangerous direction: a deleted FG row left in the mirror keeps
promising stock that no longer physically exists.

rows._why: messy but UNAMBIGUOUS — lower-case brand and string-typed warna/th must land on the SAME sku_key as FG-0001, whose JSON sends them as a number
unreadable qty must become 0, never NaN (numeric column would reject NaN)
no primary key — unkeyable, dropped and counted
A22: both quantities are separator-ambiguous. Under auto they are refused (qty -> 0, qty_m2 -> null), counted, and logged once per run.

X11: 'NaN'::numeric and 'Infinity'::numeric are LEGAL in Postgres and the schema does not forbid them in th/th_panel/p/l. One stored there would make erp_sku_key() render 'NaN' while canonicalSkuKey() renders '-', silently desynchronising that SKU. None may be written.
FIX 6: deleted upstream. Mirroring it would add 5,000 lembar of stock that does not exist — the over-promising direction.
